This new architecture integrates the voltage step-up, balancing, and charging functions inside a single converter topology to present a cost-effective and an energy efficient solution. The step-up function is obtained using assisting conversion concept and hence high power processing efficiency and small converter volume are achieved. The operation of the system is regulated by a hardware-efficient digital controller that provides control of all of the three functions at the same time. Experimental results obtained with a 24-to-48V, 200W, 100 KHz converter for small scooters demonstrate that the assisting DAB converter is capable of providing the three previously mentioned functions while running at a peak efficiency of 95.4% and processing only a 50% of the output power.

articleTitle: Optimized Power Semiconductors for the Power Electronics Based HVDC Breaker Application
publicationTitle: Proceedings of PCIM Europe 2015; International Exhibition and Conference for Power Electronics, Intelligent Motion, Renewable Energy and Energy Management
abstract: In the field of power electronics applications, advances in high voltage semiconductor devices have led specifically over the past few decades to tremendous improvements in terms of power handling capability and control. We focus in this paper on the recent developments with regard to optimizing the power semiconductor for the solid state HVDC breaker for HVDC grid applications. One of the traditional approaches for the development of power semiconductors is to achieve full integration of the active power semiconductor switch and the anti-parallel freewheeling diode. The main aim for such a trend is to obtain higher power densities and more compact systems while at the same time simplifying the component manufacturability by eliminating the need for a separate anti-parallel diode. Recent development efforts over the past few years targeted a fully integrated high voltage and high current IGBT and diode structure on a single chip. As a result, an RC-IGBT type device was realized recently and referred to as the Bi-mode Insulated Gate Transistor BIGT. The BIGT was designed in accordance with the latest IGBT design concepts while fully incorporating an optimized integrated anti-parallel diode in the IGBT structure. This paper will mainly focus on the application of the BIGT especially for the power electronics based Hybrid HVDC breaker application while presenting an overview of the recent advancements from the device design and performance viewpoint. Recent experimental data obtained from tests carried out on prototype samples will also be presented.

articleTitle: A fault tolerant communication interface for modular and distributed power electronics
publicationTitle: Proceedings of PCIM Europe 2015; International Exhibition and Conference for Power Electronics, Intelligent Motion, Renewable Energy and Energy Management
abstract: This work focuses on the design and the implementation details of a communication interface for distributed power electronic actuators. For this purpose, first the specific requirements, needed in such an area, are presented in detail. Afterwards several implementations of the hardware layer are shown and discussed regarding their characteristic in the power electronics environment. Furthermore the handling of possible transmission errors and its specific correction mechanisms is presented. Therefore typical communication errors are introduced. Their relevance will be discussed on the basis of measurements. Subsequently possible correction methods are presented and compared with respect to their implementation complexity and efficiency. Finally this paper presents the results of an experimental network and demonstrates the performance of the fault tolerant communication.

articleTitle: New Low Loss Thyristor for HVDC Transmission
publicationTitle: Proceedings of PCIM Europe 2015; International Exhibition and Conference for Power Electronics, Intelligent Motion, Renewable Energy and Energy Management
abstract: Four inch thyristor in the package with 100 mm pole piece was developed and fully qualified for 8.5 kV voltage class. The maximal ON-state voltage has been reduced from VTmax = 1.95 V to VTmax = 1.70 V at IT = 1.5 kA and T = 90 deg C. Significant reduction of leakage current extended the blocking stability up to 115deg C. The device proved its robustness and lowered losses during valve testing in 6-pulse back-to-back synthetic test circuit. The reduction of valve losses is estimated at 6 to 8 %. The 3rd Generation of PCTs for HVDC from ABB is established.

articleTitle: Photovoltaic - Wind Energy - Hybrid System with Battery and Heat-Storage Path
publicationTitle: Proceedings of PCIM Europe 2015; International Exhibition and Conference for Power Electronics, Intelligent Motion, Renewable Energy and Energy Management
abstract: The paper presents a simulation tool and latest results of an optimizing design and energy management concept for a decentralized, grid-connected photovoltaic (PV) - wind energy - hybrid system with a lead-acid- and/or lithium-ion-battery and a heat-storage path. The paper starts with an introduction, in which the principle structure of the decentralized management concept is briefly explained. The second part is a discussion of the time series of PV and wind energy supply and electricity demand (for a household application) on the basis of long-term measurement data for different reference objects. First goal is to demonstrate the supplementary nature of PV and wind power and to estimate the self-sufficiency-rates achievable without energy storage. This analysis is undertaken for different ratios of installed PV and wind power. Results for six different small wind energy turbines (SWT) and various mast heights are presented.The third part of the paper introduces a novel energy management with a peak-shaving-/power-to-heat-concept and a battery storage system. It is demonstrated that the selfsufficiency-rates can be increased up to ca. 90% by the usage of a hybrid battery storage system and an intelligent energy management concept. Simulation results are presented for a four-dimensional economic optimization of a combination of a PV plant and a small wind energy turbine relating to battery capacities, max. battery power, max. grid power and profits. Finally, six different hybrid system configurations are compared in reference to self-sufficiency-rate, investment costs, avoided electricity costs and profits.

articleTitle: Using the Zth(t) - power pulse measurement to detect a degradation in the module structure
publicationTitle: Proceedings of PCIM Europe 2015; International Exhibition and Conference for Power Electronics, Intelligent Motion, Renewable Energy and Energy Management
abstract: The electrification in the field of vehicles is progressing immensely. Therefore, power electronics plays an increasingly role. To guarantee a high reliability of the devices, health monitoring functions included into the inverter block are of interest. This paper describes a short pulse quasi-Zth-method to measure the state-of-health of the power switches in the vehicle without any external equipment. The method, which will be presented, just needs an optimized driver circuitry.

articleTitle: Control Method for One Frequency Converter Driving Two Induction Generators
publicationTitle: Proceedings of PCIM Europe 2015; International Exhibition and Conference for Power Electronics, Intelligent Motion, Renewable Energy and Energy Management
abstract: This paper shows an approach for operating two induction generators with one frequency converter. With a stator flux-oriented speed-sensor less control method the torques of the two generators can be controlled. The flux estimator is based on voltage model observers. The estimation error is minimized by using an adapted low pass filter. The control strategy has been simulated, and validated on a test bench. The test bench consists of two load machines and two 15kW generators which are controlled with a free programmable frequency converter.

articleTitle: Autonomous method of maximum power efficiency tracking for PFC- and DC/DC-converter system
publicationTitle: Proceedings of PCIM Europe 2015; International Exhibition and Conference for Power Electronics, Intelligent Motion, Renewable Energy and Energy Management
abstract: Maintaining high power efficiency across entire load range for an off-line supply system consisting of PFC- and DC/DC converter is a challenge. This is because the power efficiency behaviours of PFC- and DC/DC converters are non-linear functions of their output load level. Intelligent adjustment of intermediate bus voltage level (IBV) can help increasing power efficiency of both PFC- and DC/DC converters for entire load range. This paper shows a smart system consisting of an AC/DC PFC- and DC/DC converter providing 230Vac to 12Vdc conversion with power efficiency autonomous self-tuning algorithm. The key approaches for optimum efficiency is dynamically optimization of intermediate bus voltage.

articleTitle: Power Module Boasts highest power density in its class
publicationTitle: Proceedings of PCIM Europe 2015; International Exhibition and Conference for Power Electronics, Intelligent Motion, Renewable Energy and Energy Management
abstract: Integrated power modules are filling an urgent need in modern electronic designs where extremely compact size is needed coupled with high efficiency and abundance of features for control, monitoring and on the fly customization like voltage margining, soft start/soft shutdown and PFM/PWM selection and ease of design. This paper will primarily deal with the thermal design, simulation and testing. We will discuss how this thermal design ties together all the features that this module offers like flexibility, programmability and digital control commands and advanced features. The thermal images will support the design criteria of highest power density in its class.

articleTitle: Ultra Long Lifetime Energy Storage System using Flywheels and Matrix Converters
publicationTitle: Proceedings of PCIM Europe 2015; International Exhibition and Conference for Power Electronics, Intelligent Motion, Renewable Energy and Energy Management
abstract: The paper proposes an energy storage system (ESS) with ultra long lifetime of over 20 years using matrix converters and FWs (Flywheels) to compensate frequency and voltage fluctuation of the power grid. The FWs in the system adopt the pivot bearing, which is one of the levitation bearing to avoid attrition of the FW bearings. The FWs provide maintenance-free for over 20years. A matrix converter is used for the naturally-cooled to realize ultra long lifetime. Experimental results and loss analysis are given in order to demonstrate advantages of the proposed ESS.
